comment: Took for understanding/managing risk. Great teacher, clear expectations, fair grading, and engaging lectures. Grading comprised 4 essays and a 3000word final project, but we had lots of time for each one and could choose any topic relevant to the assignment. Tells you exactly what to include and how to structure it to get an A
She is a nice person. Even though the FYS need 4 essays and a 3000word final project, we are free to choose anything we like to wrtie. Also we did lots of presentation.

Dr. Thekdi is super nice, and the homework is really helpful for reviewing for the test. One big thing to keep in mind is submitting the class work at the end of the class every time since the class work is what composes your grades. The exams are mostly derived from the homework, and she is willing to help you to be good in exams and her classes.

Professor Thekdi is the best option for MGMT 225. Homework is optional but should be utilized for studying for tests. Exams are not incredibly difficult, but make sure you apply yourself. I actually really enjoyed the final project and if you do the work and show up to class, an A is definitely attainable.

Dr. Thekdi is the best choice for MGMT 225. She was very clear and always willing to help confused students, both in class and in office hours. The homework is optional but it is the best way to study for the tests. Very caring and a relatively easy course if you keep up with the material.
Very approachable and helpful professor. She is experienced teaching bstats.

There's only one test so if you don't do well on that then you're out of luck. She doesn't explain anything well so you have to teach yourself. Tests are much harder than quizzes, homework, or anything she does in class.
Bstat is not a difficult class and Prof. Thekdi is a good choice for this class.
We have a nice atmosphere in class with everyone discussing so we have lots of opportunities to partiocipate. I wish my other classes in the bschool were more like this.
Smart and very helpful in office hours, I got an A.

Thekdi is not a good teacher. If you do not thoroughly read the textbook sections, you will not learn anything. You essentially have to teach yourself the material outside of class, then just follow a couple of Thekdi's examples in class. I don't like her as a person either, but that may just be me. Take any other professor you can.
It's a fun class so far .she was helpful in office hours

First half of the year was easy and the midterm was easy, but then it got really hard. Must keep up with the reading, homework, and pay attention in class for the second half and definitely ask for help. Group project wasn't bad. Don't know the grade, but if definitely helped my final grade.
Don't like her personally

Very helpful and very smart person. She is one of my favorite professors in UR. Taught me a lot. Only two exams given in the class: midterm is really fine, but final is not easy. (if you do well in the midterm and CBL, final would not matter that much anyway)
She's smart and helpful. Go to class, do the assigned work, ask questions, really understand the material and you'll be fine

Attendance is mandatory, and there are weekly quizzes. Tests are pretty straightforward if you've done the homework and in class worksheets, although the final is hard. The CBL project is time consuming but do-able. She's extremely smart, presents the material well, and is willing to help in office hours.
Prof Thekdi is one of my favorite professors at UR. You can't slack off at all. Every class matters... but she is super helpful and doesn't let any question go unanswered. I loved my cbl project too.
Professor Thekdi will challenge you. Attend every class and you will end the semester a better person.
Mandatory attendance every class!!! If you are late for her takes quick attendance, she will count you as absence. Boring class and hard tests. Just don't take her class
